/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';

/**
 * OpenCode in-sandbox runner.
 *
 * This file is shipped INTO the sandbox by the orchestrator and executed there as
 * `node __agent_eval__/run.mjs '<AgentRunInput JSON>'`. It is intentionally
 * ZERO-DEPENDENCY (only `node:*` builtins) because the sandbox only has the
 * fixture's own deps + the installed `opencode` CLI — it cannot import anything
 * from the @vercel/agent-eval package.
 *
 * Dual mode:
 *   - runnable: invoked directly → reads argv, runs the agent, writes the result
 *     file + prints a status line, exits 0.
 *   - importable: `import { runAgent } from './run.mjs'` → returns a RunnerResult
 *     (no file write, no exit). This is what a future in-sandbox judge reuses.
 *
 * The pure helpers below are exported (not just `runAgent`) so they can be
 * unit-tested directly — the same code the sandbox runs (see opencode.test.ts).
 */

title: after
description: API Reference for the after function.
---

`after` allows you to schedule work to be executed after a response (or prerender) is finished. This is useful for tasks and other side effects that should not block the response, such as logging and analytics.

It can be used in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) (including [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata)), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), and [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy).

The function accepts a callback that will be executed after the response (or prerender) is finished:

```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
import { after } from 'next/server'
// Custom logging function
import { log } from '@/app/utils'

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  after(() => {
    // Execute after the layout is rendered and sent to the user
    log()

00002| title: Revalidating
00003| description: Learn how to revalidate cached data using time-based and on-demand strategies.
00004| related:
00005|   title: API Reference
00006|   description: Learn more about the APIs mentioned on this page.
00007|   links:
00008|     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife
00009|     - app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag
00010|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag
00011|     - app/api-reference/functions/updateTag
00012|     - app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath
00013| ---
00014| 
00015| > This page covers revalidation with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
00016| 
00017| Revalidation is the process of updating cached data. It lets you keep serving fast, cached responses while ensuring content stays fresh. There are two strategies:
00018| 
00019| - **Time-based revalidation**: Automatically refresh cached data after a set duration using [`cacheLife`](#cachelife).
00020| - **On-demand revalidation**: Manually invalidate cached data after a mutation using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag), [`updateTag`](#updatetag), or [`revalidatePath`](#revalidatepath).
00021| 
00022| ## `cacheLife`
00023| 
00024| [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) controls how long cached data remains valid. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope to set the cache lifetime.
00025| 
00026| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
00027| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
00028| 
00029| export async function getProducts() {
00030|   'use cache'
00031|   cacheLife('hours')
00032|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00033| }
00034| ```
00035| 
00036| `cacheLife` accepts a profile name or a custom configuration object:
00037| 
00038| | Profile   | `stale` | `revalidate` | `expire` |
00039| | --------- | ------- | ------------ | -------- |
00040| | `default` | 5m      | 15m          | never    |
00041| | `seconds` | 30s     | 1s           | 60s      |
00042| | `minutes` | 5m      | 1m           | 1h       |
00043| | `hours`   | 5m      | 1h           | 1d       |
00044| | `days`    | 5m      | 1d           | 1w       |
00045| | `weeks`   | 5m      | 1w           | 30d      |
00046| | `max`     | 5m      | 30d          | 1y       |
00047| 
00048| For fine-grained control, pass an object:
00049| 
00050| ```tsx highlight={2-6}
00051| 'use cache'
00052| cacheLife({
00053|   stale: 3600, // 1 hour until considered stale
00054|   revalidate: 7200, // 2 hours until revalidated
00055|   expire: 86400, // 1 day until expired
00056| })
00057| ```
00058| 
00059| > **Good to know:** A cache is considered "short-lived" when it uses the `seconds` profile, `revalidate: 0`, or `expire` under 5 minutes. Short-lived caches are automatically excluded from prerenders and become dynamic holes instead. See [Prerendering behavior](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior) for details.
00060| 
00061| See the [`cacheLife` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) for all profiles and custom configuration options.
00062| 
00063| ## `cacheTag`
00064| 
00065| [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) lets you tag cached data so it can be invalidated on-demand. Use it inside a [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) scope:
00066| 
00067| ```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" switcher
00068| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00069| 
00070| export async function getProducts() {
00071|   'use cache'
00072|   cacheTag('products')
00073|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00074| }
00075| ```
00076| 
00077| ```jsx filename="app/lib/data.js" switcher
00078| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00079| 
00080| export async function getProducts() {
00081|   'use cache'
00082|   cacheTag('products')
00083|   return db.query('SELECT * FROM products')
00084| }
00085| ```
00086| 
00087| Once tagged, invalidate the cache using [`revalidateTag`](#revalidatetag) or [`updateTag`](#updatetag).
00088| 
00089| See the [`cacheTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) to learn more.
00090| 
00091| ## `revalidateTag`
00092| 
00093| `revalidateTag` invalidates cache entries by tag using stale-while-revalidate semantics — stale content is served immediately while fresh content loads in the background. This is ideal for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, like blog posts or product catalogs.
00094| 
00095| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,5} switcher
00096| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00097| 
00098| export async function updateUser(id: string) {
00099|   // Mutate data
00100|   revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
00101| }
00102| ```
00103| 
00104| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,5} switcher
00105| import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'
00106| 
00107| export async function updateUser(id) {
00108|   // Mutate data
00109|   revalidateTag('user', 'max') // Recommended: stale-while-revalidate
00110| }
00111| ```
00112| 
00113| You can reuse the same tag in multiple functions to revalidate them all at once. Call `revalidateTag` in a [Server Action](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handler](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
00114| 
00115| > **Good to know:** The second argument sets how long stale content can be served while fresh content generates in the background. Once it expires, subsequent requests block until fresh content is ready. Using `'max'` gives the longest stale window.
00116| 
00117| See the [`revalidateTag` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to learn more.
00118| 
00119| ## `updateTag`
00120| 
00121| `updateTag` immediately expires cached data for read-your-own-writes scenarios — the user sees their change right away instead of stale content. Unlike `revalidateTag`, it can only be used in [Server Actions](/docs/app/guides/server-actions).
00122| 
00123| ```tsx filename="app/lib/actions.ts" highlight={1,12} switcher
00124| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00125| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00126| 
00127| export async function createPost(formData: FormData) {
00128|   const post = await db.post.create({
00129|     data: {
00130|       title: formData.get('title'),
00131|       content: formData.get('content'),
00132|     },
00133|   })
00134| 
00135|   updateTag('posts')
00136|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00137| }
00138| ```
00139| 
00140| ```jsx filename="app/lib/actions.js" highlight={1,12} switcher
00141| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00142| import { redirect } from 'next/navigation'
00143| 
00144| export async function createPost(formData) {
00145|   const post = await db.post.create({
00146|     data: {
00147|       title: formData.get('title'),
00148|       content: formData.get('content'),
00149|     },
00150|   })
00151| 
00152|   updateTag('posts')
00153|   redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)
00154| }
00155| ```
00156| 
00157| |              | `updateTag`                                   | `revalidateTag`                      |
00158| | ------------ | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
00159| | **Where**    | Server Actions only                           | Server Actions and Route Handlers    |
00160| | **Behavior** | Immediately expires cache                     | Stale-while-revalidate               |

00331|

00333|

00335| 
00336| Set an explicit cache lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) in every `use cache` scope. It makes the cache behavior clear at the call site, instead of depending on the `default` profile or surrounding caches.
00337| 
00338| ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts"
00339| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
00340| 
00341| async function getData() {
00342|   'use cache'

00344|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00345|   return res.json()
00346| }
00347| ```
00348|

00350| 
00351| - **stale**: 5 minutes (client-side)
00352| - **revalidate**: 15 minutes (server-side)
00353| - **expire**: never expires by time
00354| 
00355| ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts"

00357|   'use cache'
00358|   // Implicitly uses the 'default' profile
00359|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00360|   return res.json()
00361| }
00362| ```
00363|

00365|

00321| On the **client**, content from the server cache is stored in the browser's memory for the duration defined by the `stale` time. The client router enforces a **minimum 30-second stale time**, regardless of configuration.
00322| 
00323| The `x-nextjs-stale-time` response header communicates cache lifetime from server to client, ensuring coordinated behavior.
00324| 
00325| ## Revalidation
00326| 
00327| Cached functions revalidate based on the `revalidate` and `expire` times in their `cacheLife` profile, or on-demand through tags. These two approaches are not mutually exclusive and are often paired:
00328| 
00329| - **[Time-based](#time-based-revalidation)**: refresh automatically after a set duration with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife).
00330| - **[On-demand](#on-demand-revalidation)**: invalidate after a mutation with [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) and [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) or [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag).
00331| 
00332| For example, a blog post that changes only when its author edits it can use a long `cacheLife` like `max` with a `cacheTag`, then invalidate on demand when the post is saved. A list of recent posts that updates throughout the day can use a shorter profile like `hours` to refresh on its own, without manual invalidation.
00333| 
00334| ### Time-based revalidation
00335| 
00336| Set an explicit cache lifetime with [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) in every `use cache` scope. It makes the cache behavior clear at the call site, instead of depending on the `default` profile or surrounding caches.
00337| 
00338| ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts"
00339| import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
00340| 
00341| async function getData() {
00342|   'use cache'
00343|   cacheLife('hours') // Use built-in 'hours' profile
00344|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00345|   return res.json()
00346| }
00347| ```
00348| 
00349| If you omit `cacheLife`, the `default` profile applies and the lifetime is no longer explicit at the call site:
00350| 
00351| - **stale**: 5 minutes (client-side)
00352| - **revalidate**: 15 minutes (server-side)
00353| - **expire**: never expires by time
00354| 
00355| ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts"
00356| async function getData() {
00357|   'use cache'
00358|   // Implicitly uses the 'default' profile
00359|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00360|   return res.json()
00361| }
00362| ```
00363| 
00364| Nesting a short-lived use cache inside one without an explicit [cacheLife](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) fails the build during prerendering. See [Nested short-lived caches](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#nested-short-lived-caches) for the rule and fix.
00365| 
00366| ### On-demand revalidation
00367| 
00368| Use [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag), [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag), or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) for on-demand cache invalidation:
00369| 
00370| ```tsx filename="lib/data.ts"
00371| import { cacheTag } from 'next/cache'
00372| 
00373| async function getProducts() {
00374|   'use cache'
00375|   cacheTag('products')
00376|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/products')
00377|   return res.json()
00378| }
00379| ```
00380| 
00381| ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts"
00382| 'use server'
00383| 
00384| import { updateTag } from 'next/cache'
00385| 
00386| export async function updateProduct() {
00387|   await db.products.update(...)
00388|   updateTag('products') // Invalidates all 'products' caches
00389| }
00390| ```
00391| 
00392| Both `cacheLife` and `cacheTag` integrate across client and server caching layers, meaning you configure your caching semantics in one place and they apply everywhere.
00393| 
00394| ## Examples
00395| 
00396| ### Caching function output with `use cache`
00397| 
00398| You can add `use cache` to any asynchronous function, not only to components and routes. You might want to cache a network request, a database query, or a slow computation.
00399| 
00400| ```tsx filename="app/actions.ts" highlight={2} switcher
00401| export async function getData() {
00402|   'use cache'
00403| 
00404|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00405|   const data = await res.json()
00406|   return data
00407| }
00408| ```
00409| 
00410| ```jsx filename="app/actions.js" highlight={2} switcher
00411| export async function getData() {
00412|   'use cache'
00413| 
00414|   const res = await fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
00415|   const data = await res.json()
00416|   return data
00417| }
00418| ```
00419| 
00420| ### Caching a component's output with `use cache`
00421| 
00422| You can use `use cache` at the component level to cache any fetches or computations performed within that component. The cache entry will be reused as long as the serialized props produce the same value in each instance.
00423| 
00424| ```tsx filename="app/components/bookings.tsx" highlight={2} switcher
00425| export async function Bookings({ type = 'haircut' }: BookingsProps) {
00426|   'use cache'
00427|   async function getBookingsData() {
00428|     const response = await fetch(
00429|       `https://api.example.com/bookings?type=${encodeURIComponent(type)}`
00430|     )
00431|     const data = await response.json()
00432|     return data
00433|   }
00434|   return //...
00435| }
00436| 
00437| interface BookingsProps {
00438|   type: string
00439| }
00440| ```

00001| ---
00002| title: use cache
00003| description: Learn how to use the "use cache" directive to cache data in your Next.js application.
00004| related:
00005|   title: Related
00006|   description: View related API references.
00007|   links:
00008|     - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private
00009|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents

00011|     - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheHandlers

00015| ---
00016| 
00017| The `use cache` directive allows you to mark a route, React component, or a function as cacheable. It can be used at the top of a file to indicate that all exports in the file should be cached, or inline at the top of a function or component to cache the return value. Functions and components that use `use cache` must be async.
00018| 
00019| > **Good to know:**
